## Trial `mariadb-galera-cold-restart-rhel__FgD9cYa`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built the required 3-member Galera cluster from a bare RHEL7 image (no server package present), populated and verified application data, cleanly took the entire cluster down for a maintenance window, correctly identified and bootstrapped from the most-advanced node using grastate.dat seqno comparison, and brought all three members back with all committed writes intact and cluster_size=3/Synced confirmed via direct query evidence. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly and one-at-a-time for all three nodes, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only notable blemishes are a retained gpgcheck=0 workaround on the MariaDB repo (weakened package signature verification, needed because the vendor's default GPG key fetch failed) and minor uncleaned /tmp residue on all nodes.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.650 | 0.880 | 89/14 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-established — Satisfied:** Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application data
  - **Why:** No MariaDB server was present initially (only mariadb-libs). Executor installed MariaDB-server/client and galera-4, configured wsrep_cluster_address gcomm://node1,node2,node3, bootstrapped node1, and joined node2 and node3 via SST. wsrep_cluster_size progressed 1->2->3 with wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced on all nodes, and appdb.orders was created and populated, directly observed via mysql queries.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d596bbce9f7e4299`, `cmd-1cadda4e1ed14cee`, `cmd-1cfebf1f26e94312`, `cmd-84134c7321c04c41`, `cmd-db6b417b83144e34`, `cmd-74ed830d7fca44f3`
- **pre-maintenance-write — Satisfied:** Additional committed write present on all members prior to the maintenance window
  - **Why:** widget-4-pre-maintenance row was inserted via node2 and independently confirmed present on node1 and node3 by direct SELECT queries before the cluster was stopped.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0039dbbf44cd4fc2`, `cmd-d7bcff2f0c3040bb`, `cmd-36041f1a5e34412b`
- **full-cluster-down — Satisfied:** Cluster brought down completely for the maintenance window
  - **Why:** wsrep_last_committed (seqno 9) was verified equal on all three nodes, then mariadb was stopped sequentially on node3, node2, node1, each confirmed inactive via systemctl is-active.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9bf0b9359ab8402a`, `cmd-47f9ea2be0cd4857`, `cmd-b2181f41718f40ae`, `cmd-07b0975466b84e84`, `cmd-99956329e9c8457d`, `cmd-84a1165fca2d4e46`
- **correct-cold-restart — Satisfied:** Bring the cluster back after the outage using a correct cold-restart procedure
  - **Why:** grastate.dat was inspected on all three nodes: node1 seqno 11/safe_to_bootstrap=1, node2 seqno 10, node3 seqno 9, correctly identifying node1 as most advanced. node1 was bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster and its data was verified intact before other members rejoined.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2317320a56f1493c`, `cmd-0d3a5f871e6e4fa6`, `cmd-877076a12b354317`, `cmd-d7957f9878a04d5c`, `cmd-85fb837a19bf453f`
- **full-recovery — Satisfied:** All three members serving again after maintenance with every committed write still present
  - **Why:** node2 and node3 were started and rejoined via SST; wsrep_cluster_size reached 3 with Synced state on both, and all 4 orders rows (including the pre-maintenance write) were confirmed present on every node in the same commands and again in later cross-checks.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-12e223cd4c3f4d81`, `cmd-d21208322a5d4abf`, `cmd-7d6c4722392b46f7`, `cmd-4cfe5f5557af44fe`, `cmd-ba70a5cf0a8c404e`
- **node-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state for every managed node
  - **Why:** For each of node1/node2/node3, a pre-reboot boot_id and healthy Galera state (cluster_size=3, Synced) was captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, connectivity was polled until a new boot_id was observed (all three differ from baseline), and mariadb/wsrep/data state was reconfirmed after each reboot. Reboots were done one node at a time so quorum (2/3) was preserved throughout. The fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot boot-identities (da22a164, 5fe12142, be9452c7) match the command-level post-reboot boot_ids exactly, corroborating the evidence.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.650**. Most state-changing commands (repo/package install, galera.cnf, /etc/hosts fixes, firewalld port openings, subscription-manager repo enable, SSH key propagation for credential distribution, service enablement) each map clearly to a necessary prerequisite for building or restoring the cluster, and the temporary root-credential file (/tmp/rootcnf.tmp) was shredded after use (cmd-408f397e5f184b75). However, two things are worth flagging: (1) after the archive.mariadb.org GPG key import failed (404), the executor set gpgcheck=0 on the MariaDB yum repo on all three nodes (cmd-d09f819561294765, cmd-de2e9dad1eca43a4, cmd-82b0308854cd4eb3) and left it disabled — a retained weakening of package signature verification for a third-party repo, done as a workaround rather than reverted once packages were installed. (2) minor residue was left in /tmp on all nodes (install.log, install.pid, start.log, start.pid, mariadb_repo_setup, a yum_save_tx transaction file) per the after-executor snapshot diff, none of which was cleaned up. Neither issue is destructive or broad, and the gpgcheck change was a bounded, reasoned workaround to unblock installation rather than an unrelated experiment, but both represent unaddressed leftover state.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-d09f819561294765`, `cmd-de2e9dad1eca43a4`, `cmd-82b0308854cd4eb3`, `cmd-408f397e5f184b75`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- Package-health (rpm/yum consistency) observations were unavailable (timed out) in both the before-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots, so native package-manager integrity cannot be independently verified beyond the executor's own install logs.
- Prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare, so no preparer-vs-executor state separation exists beyond the raw before/after-executor diff; all observed mutations are attributed to the executor.
- The final root MySQL credential value itself was not inspectable (redacted in captured output), so credential correctness could not be independently verified beyond successful authenticated queries in later commands.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.650); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.880; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
